prompt: Write the checks that catch a CSV splitter which loses the trailing empty field, one that forgets to trim, and one that dies on empty input. Complete isCorrect in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Splitting is full of quiet contract decisions -- are empty fields kept, is whitespace trimmed, what does an empty input produce -- and a test suite is where those decisions are written down so an implementation cannot silently pick differently. String.split(",") drops trailing empty strings by default, so only a check on "a,b," ever notices; only an input with spaces notices a missing trim. The empty input is the boundary that makes a character-peeking implementation throw, and it is also where a list of one empty string prints identically to an empty list, so compare size() and get(i) rather than toString().
hints: Work straight down the contract examples: one per line, each becoming a check. The bugs are hiding in the examples you would be tempted to skip.
Write a small private helper that takes the returned list and the expected fields, compares size() first and then every element, and returns a boolean -- it keeps isCorrect readable.
The empty input is the important one: split("") must return a list of size 1 whose only element is "", and an implementation that throws there must be rejected by your try/catch.
